summary:
A preview of the DEF CON 20 documentary project. A sneak peek into the official DEF CON 20 documentary, featuring previews of the conference's 20-year history and cultural evolution.

(AI summary — Claude Haiku)

Historical Origins and Community Ethos

Filmed with unprecedented full access during DEF CON 20 in Las Vegas, director Jason Scott chronicles the evolution of the world's largest hacker conference from a 100-person farewell party in 1993 into a global cultural institution.

Inside the Four Days of DEF CON

The documentary captures the kinetic energy and subterranean culture across the convention floor, exploring capture-the-flag competitions, lockpicking villages, hardware badge assembly, and live research disclosures.

The People Behind the Lore

Through candid interviews with founder Jeff Moss (The Dark Tangent), volunteer goons, long-time attendees, and federal observers, the film documents the human stories, mischief, and mutual respect holding the diverse hacker community together.

Legacy and Independence

The film explores why DEF CON maintains strict operational independence, preserving an authentic hacker gathering defined by curiosity, freedom of inquiry, and communal self-governance.
